newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids steady to up on crude rally.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids steady to up on crude rally.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices, helped by a sharp rally in crude, were steady to up slightly Monday in thin trade, but few expected much more upside, with mild weather still hampering utility demand.

"With crude up and paper quoted higher, sellers are not discounting physical oil, but there's still not a lot of demand and I don't see that changing this week," said one cash trader, noting forecasts for fairly mild East Coast weather.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent gained a quarter to $15.25-50 a barrel, with May paper done 25 cents higher at $15.85 on stronger crude, traders said.
NYH June one percent paper jumped almost 50 cents to $16.40-55, while July and August were quoted at $16.55-70.

Traders said the steep run in paper helped boost some physical grades, particularly low sulphurs which could also gain from some utility fuel switching from more expensive gas when better cooling loads kick in.

But the weather offered little immediate help for the bulls, with Northeast and Mid-Atlantic temperatures this week not expected to vary much from normal, and the South expected to start the week below-normal, then warm to near-normal.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour notionally firmed slightly to $16.00-25, traders said.
New York high sulphurs were steady from Friday, with 2.2 percent still pegged at about $14.50.
At the U.S. Gulf, three percent remained pegged at about $14, with June paper sold higher at $14.25. USG one percent was unchanged at $14.75.

New York city gate swing gas prices slipped a couple of cents Monday to the low-$2.50s/mmBtu, or about $15.94 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, fell a similar amount to about $2.27/mmBtu, or $14.30 a barrel.
